01 / THE BRIEF

A district, not a building

The District Detroit wasn't a single project — it was a 50-block portfolio of interdependent assets stitched into the fabric of downtown Detroit: an arena, corporate headquarters, an academic building, retail, public space, and thousands of parking spaces across new decks and existing lots.

My role was to hold the whole thing together strategically — running portfolio management and owner's representation across the assets, so decisions on any one piece accounted for the others and for the district as a whole.

02B / CONCEPT → BUILT

From rendering to reality

The Global Resource Center — Little Caesars' world headquarters, designed by HOK as architect of record — moved from concept rendering to a built landmark on Woodward Avenue. On the owner's side I served as owner's representative and led design management, stewarding the diagrid glass facade and stepped terraces from rendering to realized.

03 / THE WORK

What I led

Across four years, the work spanned the full pre-development and delivery arc — from feasibility and entitlement through consultant selection, contract negotiation, and design management. Properties were analyzed under both GMP and Lump Sum methodologies to test cost certainty across the portfolio.

Portfolio Management Strategic Planning Urban Design Feasibility Entitlement Pre-Construction Consultant Selection Contract Negotiation Budgeting & Estimating Design Management Tenant Coordination
